subject: Post-demo snapshot: finalists, tradeoffs, and recommended next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Diaz <cdiaz@orionai.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo snapshot: finalists, tradeoffs, and recommended next steps

Hi Clara / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a recommended shortlist based on the demo workload (multi-turn customer support + retrieval augmentation). I kept this tight so you can share with your ML/infra folks.

1) Primary problem we heard you want solved:
- Low-latency (p95 < 300ms) responses for guided support flows, while keeping per-conversation cost predictable.
- Risk: factual hallucination on domain-specific policies and occasional long-context reasoning (past 2 turns).

2) Shortlist (recommended order) + rationale (quality / latency / cost):
- Atlas-6B-INT8 (option A) — Recommended canary. p95 ~ 140ms, ~ $0.18 / 1k tokens, human eval 82/100 on our delta prompt set. Best-in-class for latency and cost; small drop on complex multi-step reasoning (observed ~6% lower exact-match on policy extraction tasks).
- NorthStar-14B-q4_0 (option B) — Balanced choice. p95 ~ 320ms, ~ $0.42 / 1k tokens, human eval 89/100. Strong reasoning and fewer hallucinations; cost and latency higher but within your target if routed selectively.
- Vanguard-30B-ptq (option C) — Highest quality. p95 ~ 750ms, ~ $1.20 / 1k tokens, human eval 94/100. Use for tiered escalation paths (agent assist / sensitive answers) where accuracy matters more than latency.

3) Key tradeoffs we observed (from the benchmark CSV attached):
- Latency vs cost: Atlas is ~3–4x cheaper than Vanguard but incurs drop on complex-policy extraction; NorthStar is a middle ground.
- Regression risk: Atlas showed a recurring pattern of concise but occasionally incomplete extractions—this is a prompt/temperature tuning case but also an architectural limit for very small-context models.
- Tail latency: Vanguard has higher p99s on cold KV-cache hits; we recommend warm-prefix caching for escalation flows.

4) Proposed evaluation plan (short, 2-week cadence):
- Week 0 (now): share the prompt_set_v1.txt and 250 labeled examples (we attached). You run on your infra or use our shared notebook.
- Week 1: run A/B on Atlas vs NorthStar for the canonical user flows (50k tokens each). We’ll provide the eval harness and scripts in the Colab link.
- Week 2: human-in-the-loop review on ~200 edge cases; decide routing policy (e.g., Atlas default, NorthStar for medium-confidence, Vanguard for low-confidence/high-risk).

5) Immediate asks from us (can you):
- Confirm who on your side will run the Colab (name + email) and whether you want us to provision a short Redwood trial with the three model variants.
- Flag any compliance constraints (PII, retention) that would require Private deployment instead of Hosted.

Attachments: orion_demo-benchmarks-20270528.csv (benchmarks), prompt_set_v1.txt (eval prompts), shortlist_reco_onepager.pdf (slides).

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

On Fri, 28 May 2027 at 09:40, Clara Diaz <cdiaz@orionai.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — super clear summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: \n> 
> 1) For the Atlas run, are you using temperature 0.2 and the 2048 token context? If so, can you also try temp=0.0? We suspect the model is over-confident on shorter answers.
> 
> 2) For NorthStar, can you share whether the eval used the same retrieval embedding cutoff? Our infra currently truncates retrieved docs at 1k tokens.
> 
> We’ll loop in Pranav (ML eng) to run your Colab — he’s out until Monday but will take this first thing. Also, compliance: we have standard SOC2 + internal retention policy (30 days), no PII expected for this trial.
> 
> Clara
>

From: Clara Diaz <cdiaz@orionai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionai.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo snapshot: finalists, tradeoffs, and recommended next steps

Ben —

Appreciate the write-up. Quick answers: we will run Colab internally (Pranav is the owner) and can take the Atlas temp=0.0 run. Retrieval cutoff is 1k — worth testing a larger window for the policy extraction flows.

Two asks from us:
- If you can, include the human-eval rubric (how scores map to risk buckets).
- Can Redwood provision a 7-day dedicated Canary so we can see production-like latency?

Clara

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Diaz <cdiaz@orionai.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo snapshot: finalists, tradeoffs, and recommended next steps

Clara — thanks. Quick updates:

- Attached the human-eval rubric as page 2 of the onepager and included score-to-risk mapping in the Colab (link above). Short summary: 85+ = low risk, 70–84 = moderate risk (needs spot checks), <70 = high risk (route to Vanguard / human review).
- We can provision a 7-day Canary on Dedicated: I’ve opened OPP-2027-0897-CANARY and added Lauren to the flow for provisioning. To proceed we need a PO or short email confirmation from your procurement team authorizing the trial (no charge, only usage monitoring).

Technical notes for your ML eng team:
- Atlas temp=0.0 reduces hallucination-prone concise answers; we saw a +4 points on the rubric but occasional verbosity loss on extraction which we can mitigate via the prompt (we suggested improved extraction marker in prompt_set_v1.txt).
- NorthStar in q4_0 uses a conservative sampling profile—good middle-ground for accuracy.
- KV cache warmup matters: for Vanguard we recommend sending a 3-turn warmup snippet for escalation flows.

Next steps / asks (internal owners):
- Lauren: coordinate Canary provisioning and confirm k8s egress controls for the trial.
- Michael: prepare the cost estimate for an expected 200k tokens/day profile (include Dedicated vs Hosted delta).

Clara / Samir — can you confirm the procurement contact and whether we should route the Canary to your staging region (us-west-2) or a shared Redwood sandbox?

Thanks,
Ben
